title: Kingdom of Westphalia
capsule: The Kingdom of Westphalia was a Napoleonic client state created by the Treaty of Tilsit in 1807 from territories wrested from Prussia, Hesse-Kassel, and Brunswick, with Napoleon's youngest brother Jérôme Bonaparte installed as king. Napoleon designed it as a model reform state: it received the first written constitution in German history, abolished serfdom, extended legal equality to Jews under laws of 1808, and introduced the Napoleonic Code and the metric system. Heavy military obligations proved catastrophic — Westphalian forces sent into Russia in 1812 were virtually annihilated, and the kingdom was bankrupt by year's end. Following Napoleon's defeat at the Battle of Leipzig, Prussian troops occupied the kingdom on 26 October 1813, restoring its former rulers; most of Jérôme's social reforms nonetheless persisted under the successor states.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is very well attested; the kingdom's borders were formally defined by treaty and documented in Napoleonic-era cartography.
